title: Why Does Canada Speak French and English?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: belonging to the original inhabitants of a place before outsiders arrived
continuing to support a person, country, or organisation
a language that is legally recognised by a government
completely independent and able to govern itself
the idea or policy that different cultures should be respected and encouraged within one society
the process of moving to another country to live permanently
the characteristics, history, and culture that define a person, group, or country

sentences.en: Why does Canada speak both English and French?
sentences.zh: 为什么加拿大既说英语又说法语？

sentences.en: Why is Canada’s head of state the King of the United Kingdom?
sentences.zh: 为什么加拿大的国家元首是英国国王？

sentences.en: Why didn’t Canada become part of the United States when the rest of Britain’s North American colonies rebelled?
sentences.zh: 当英国的其他北美殖民地起义时，为什么加拿大没有加入美国？

sentences.en: Canada is one of the largest countries on Earth.
sentences.zh: 加拿大是地球上面积最大的国家之一。

sentences.en: It stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific, and all the way north to the Arctic.
sentences.zh: 它从大西洋一直延伸到太平洋，并一路向北直抵北极。

sentences.en: It has one of the world’s wealthiest economies, consistently ranks among the best places to live, and is often seen as one of the most multicultural societies in the world.
sentences.zh: 它拥有世界领先的经济体之一，生活质量常年名列前茅，并被普遍视为世界上最具多元文化的社会之一。

sentences.en: The history of Canada is fascinating. Indigenous peoples lived there for thousands of years before Europeans arrived.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的历史引人入胜。在欧洲人到来之前，原住民已经在那里生活了数千年。

sentences.en: It was claimed and settled by both France and Britain.
sentences.zh: 它曾被法国和英国分别宣称占领并定居。

sentences.en: It developed differently from its neighbour the United States and gradually evolved into an independent country while still having a close relationship with the British Crown.
sentences.zh: 它的发展轨迹与邻国美国不同，在与英国王室保持紧密联系的同时，逐渐演变成了一个独立的国家。

sentences.en: So, in today’s episode, we’re going to explore how Canada was formed, why English and French coexist, how Canada developed its unique relationship with Britain, and the biggest challenges shaping Canada’s future.
sentences.zh: 因此，在今天的节目中，我们将探讨加拿大的形成过程、英法两种语言为何能共存、加拿大如何与英国发展出独特的双边关系，以及塑造加拿大未来的最大挑战。

sentences.en: And we will do all of this while practicing your English listening comprehension and learning some new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 在了解这些内容的同时，大家还能练习英语听力理解并学习一些新词汇。

sentences.en: Who was living in Canada before the Europeans arrived?
sentences.zh: 在欧洲人到来之前，是谁住在加拿大？

sentences.en: For thousands of years before any European ships crossed the Atlantic, the land we now call Canada was already home to people.
sentences.zh: 在任何欧洲船只横渡大西洋的数千年前，我们如今称之为加拿大的这片土地就已经有人居住了。

sentences.en: Today, indigenous peoples in Canada are generally grouped into three categories: First Nations, Inuit, and the Métis.
sentences.zh: 如今，加拿大的原住民通常被分为三大类：第一民族（First Nations）、因纽特人（Inuit）和梅蒂人（Métis）。

sentences.en: The First Nations include hundreds of different nations spread across southern Canada.
sentences.zh: 第一民族包括分布在加拿大南部的数百个不同的族群。

sentences.en: They spoke dozens of languages and lived in many different ways, depending on their environment.
sentences.zh: 他们操着几十种语言，并根据各自的环境采取了许多不同的生活方式。

sentences.en: On the Pacific Coast, some communities relied on fishing and built wooden longhouses.
sentences.zh: 在太平洋海岸，一些社群依靠捕鱼为生，并建造了木制长屋。

sentences.en: Across the Great Plains, some nations followed the migration of the bison.
sentences.zh: 在大平原地区，一些民族跟随美洲野牛的迁徙路线生活。

sentences.en: In the eastern forests, some farmed crops like corn or beans and squash, and they also hunted and traded.
sentences.zh: 在东部森林里，一些人种植玉米、豆类或南瓜等农作物，他们也进行狩猎和贸易。

sentences.en: Further north lived the Inuit, whose communities adapted to perhaps the harshest environment on Earth… the Arctic Circle.
sentences.zh: 更往北居住的是因纽特人，他们的社群适应了地球上或许是最严酷的环境……北极圈。

sentences.en: Instead of farming, the Inuit needed to depend on hunting.
sentences.zh: 因纽特人没有从事农业，而是必须依靠狩猎维生。

sentences.en: They hunted seals and whales and caribou.
sentences.zh: 他们猎捕海豹、鲸鱼和驯鹿。

sentences.en: They also fished in the ocean. The Métis are different.
sentences.zh: 他们还在海里捕鱼。梅蒂人则有所不同。

sentences.en: They emerged later, during the period of European colonization.
sentences.zh: 他们出现得较晚，是在欧洲殖民时期。

sentences.en: The Métis are a group of people which have both indigenous and European ancestry, particularly French ancestry.
sentences.zh: 梅蒂人是一群既有原住民血统又有欧洲血统（尤其是法国血统）的人群。

sentences.en: Over time, they have made their own language called Michif.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，他们创造了自己的语言，被称为密奇夫语（Michif）。

sentences.en: I probably pronounced that wrong. These peoples, these indigenous peoples, were not primitive societies, isolated societies.
sentences.zh: 我这个发音可能不太标准。这些人，这些原住民，并不是原始社会或孤立的社会。

sentences.en: They were connected. They had trade routes that stretched for thousands of kilometers.
sentences.zh: 他们有着紧密的联系。他们拥有延伸数千公里的贸易路线。

sentences.en: This is a really important point because older history books often describe Europeans as discovering North America.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为较旧的历史书经常将欧洲人描述为“发现”了北美洲。

sentences.en: But from the perspective of the people living there already, there was nothing to discover.
sentences.zh: 但从已经生活在那里的当地人的角度来看，根本没有什么需要被发现的。

sentences.en: However, the encounter, the meeting, between indigenous peoples and European explorers changed the Americas forever.
sentences.zh: 然而，原住民与欧洲探险家之间的这种相遇和交汇，永远改变了美洲。

sentences.en: Diseases such as smallpox, which were introduced by Europeans, sometimes accidentally, sometimes on purpose, spread through indigenous communities.
sentences.zh: 天花等由欧洲人引入的疾病——有时是无意中，有时是故意的——在原住民社群中蔓延开来。

sentences.en: These communities had no immunity. They were not protected against European diseases, and enormous numbers of people died.
sentences.zh: 这些社群没有任何免疫力。他们对欧洲的疾病毫无抵抗力，无数人因此丧生。

sentences.en: In fact, many populations in Canada and other parts of the Americas had completely collapsed and disappeared before Europeans even managed to make towns or cities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至在欧洲人成功建立城镇或城市之前，加拿大和美洲其他地区的许多原住民人口就已经彻底崩溃并消亡了。

sentences.en: As European colonies expanded over the following centuries, more and more indigenous peoples were displaced, kicked out of their lands, and their independence was taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 随着欧洲殖民地在接下来的几个世纪里不断扩张，越来越多的原住民流离失所，被驱逐出自己的土地，他们的独立也遭到了剥夺。

sentences.en: The first Europeans to explore the region of modern-day Canada extensively were fishermen, usually from countries like England, France, and Portugal.
sentences.zh: 最早广泛探索现代加拿大地区的欧洲人是渔民，通常来自英国、法国和葡萄牙等国家。

sentences.en: It was the French who went on to establish the first colonies.
sentences.zh: 正是法国人率先建立了最早的殖民地。

sentences.en: In 1534, the French explorer Jacques Cartier sailed into the Gulf of Saint Lawrence.
sentences.zh: 1534年，法国探险家雅克·卡蒂亚（Jacques Cartier）航行进入圣劳伦斯湾。

sentences.en: During his voyages, he claimed the land for the French king, and he made contact with some of the indigenous peoples living along the river.
sentences.zh: 在他的航行期间，他宣布这片土地归法国国王所有，并与沿河居住的一些原住民取得了联系。

sentences.en: Cartier actually heard the local word kanata, meaning village or settlement.
sentences.zh: 卡蒂亚当时听到了当地人说的一个词“kanata”，意思是村庄或定居点。

sentences.en: Europeans started to use this word, kanata, to refer to the surrounding region.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人开始用这个词来指代周边地区。

sentences.en: And eventually, it became the name of the entire country, Canada.
sentences.zh: 最终，它成了整个国家的名称——加拿大。

sentences.en: In 1608, another French explorer, Samuel de Champlain, founded the city of Quebec.
sentences.zh: 1608年，另一位法国探险家萨缪尔·德·尚普兰（Samuel de Champlain）建立了魁北克城。

sentences.en: Champlain wanted to build a permanent colony, and this settlement, Quebec, became the center of New France.
sentences.zh: 尚普兰想要建立一个永久性的殖民地，而这个定居点魁北克，便成为了新法兰西（New France）的中心。

sentences.en: New France was France’s North American empire.
sentences.zh: 新法兰西是法国在北门的一大北美帝国。

sentences.en: For the next century, century and a half, French settlers slowly expanded along the St.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一个世纪到 一个半世纪里，法国定居者沿着圣劳伦斯河缓慢扩张。

sentences.en: Lawrence River. They created an economy based on fur, animal skins.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了一个以毛皮和动物皮革为基础的经济。

sentences.en: Wealthy Europeans loved fashionable hats made from beaver fur particularly.
sentences.zh: 富有的欧洲人格外喜爱用海狸毛皮制作的时尚帽子。

sentences.en: French traders realized they could make a really good income from the fur trade.
sentences.zh: 法国商人意识到，通过毛皮贸易，他们可以获得相当丰厚的收入。

sentences.en: They worked with many indigenous nations, swapping European goods for furs.
sentences.zh: 他们与许多原住民民族合作，用欧洲的商品换取毛皮。

sentences.en: Unlike Britain’s colonies further south, New France never attracted an enormous number of settlers.
sentences.zh: 与更南端英国的殖民地不同，新法兰西从未吸引到数量庞大的定居者。

sentences.en: It was cold. It had less economic opportunities.
sentences.zh: 那里很冷。经济机会较少。

sentences.en: There wasn’t as much farm ground or interesting places to set up towns.
sentences.zh: 没有那么多适合耕种的土地或建立城镇的有趣地方。

sentences.en: By the middle of the 18th century, only around 70,000 French settlers lived in New France.
sentences.zh: 到18世纪中叶，新法兰西仅居住着大约7万名法国定居者。

sentences.en: Compare this with the over a million people living in Britain’s American colonies.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，当时生活在英国美洲殖民地的人口超过了一百万。

sentences.en: Britain and France were fierce rivals at this time.
sentences.zh: 当时英国和法国是死敌。

sentences.en: Their rivalry eventually resulted in the Seven Years’ War.
sentences.zh: 他们的敌对最终引发了七年战争。

sentences.en: This is a conflict sometimes described as the first true global war.
sentences.zh: 这场冲突有时被描述为第一场真正的全球战争。

sentences.en: It was fought across Europe, Asia, Africa, and North America.
sentences.zh: 这场战争在欧洲、亚洲、非洲和北美洲都有交火。

sentences.en: The British defeated the French in North America, and the Treaty of Paris officially transferred New France to British control.
sentences.zh: 英国人在北美击败了法国人，《巴黎条约》正式将新法兰西划归英国管辖。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Britain found itself governing, controlling, 70,000 French-speaking Catholics, who had their own language, law system, and culture.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，英国发现自己要统治和控制7万名说法语的天主教徒，他们拥有自己的语言、法律体系和文化。

sentences.en: Britain, of course, was an English-speaking Protestant country at this time.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时的英国是一个说英语的新教国家。

sentences.en: But, instead of forcing these French-speaking Catholics to abandon their culture, Britain made a pragmatic decision, kind of surprising really.
sentences.zh: 但是，英国并没有强迫这些说法语的天主教徒放弃他们的文化，而是做出了一个务实的决定，这其实有点让人意外。

sentences.en: The Quebec Act of 1774 allowed French Canadians to continue speaking French, continue being Catholic, and also continue using French civil law in their daily life.
sentences.zh: 1774年的《魁北克法案》允许法裔加拿大人继续说法语、保持天主教信仰，并允许他们在日常生活中继续使用法国民法。

sentences.en: Just two years after this, Britain’s 13 American colonies began their revolution.
sentences.zh: 就在两年后，英国的13个美洲殖民地发动了革命。

sentences.en: Most people in Quebec remained loyal to the British Empire rather than joining the American rebels further south.
sentences.zh: 魁北克的大多数人选择效忠大英帝国，而不是加入更南边的美国叛军。

sentences.en: Britain had treated them relatively well and let them keep their culture.
sentences.zh: 英国对他们相对较好，并让他们保留了自己的文化。

sentences.en: In the USA, or what would become the USA, the religion was predominantly Protestant and quite strict in their Christianity.
sentences.zh: 在美国，或者说即将成为美国的地区，其宗教信仰主要是新教，且其基督教信仰相当严格。

sentences.en: They were English-speaking in majority, and there was no guarantee they would let Quebec remain a French-speaking Catholic province.
sentences.zh: 他们绝大多数说英语，而且没有人能保证他们会允许魁北克继续成为一个说法语的天主教省份。

sentences.en: French-speaking communities grew in Quebec.
sentences.zh: 说法语的社群在魁北克不断发展壮大。

sentences.en: Today, around one in five Canadians speak French as their first language, and Quebec remains one of the largest French-speaking places anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 今天，大约每五个加拿大人中就有一个以法语为第一语言，魁北克依然是世界上规模最大的法语区之一。

sentences.en: Quebec has a unique variety of French that has developed separately from the language spoken in modern France.
sentences.zh: 魁北克拥有独特变体的法语，它与现代法国所说的语言分头发展开来。

sentences.en: Let’s go back to the end of the Seven Years’ War.
sentences.zh: 让我们把时间拨回七年战争结束时。

sentences.en: Britain had defeated France and taken control of New France.
sentences.zh: 英国击败了法国并夺取了新法兰西的控制权。

sentences.en: The population there was still mostly French-speaking, especially along the Saint Lawrence River.
sentences.zh: 那里的人口仍然主要说法语，尤其是在圣劳伦斯河沿岸。

sentences.en: So how did English eventually become the dominant language across Canada?
sentences.zh: 那么，英语最终是如何成为整个加拿大的主流语言的呢？

sentences.en: Well, just over 10 years after Britain conquered New France, the American Revolution broke out in Britain’s North American colonies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在英国征服新法兰西后短短十几年，美国革命在英国的北美殖民地爆发了。

sentences.en: In 1776, 13 British colonies declared their independence.
sentences.zh: 1776年，13个英国殖民地宣告独立。

sentences.en: They were arguing that they should no longer be ruled by Britain.
sentences.zh: 他们争辩说，他们不应再受英国的统治。

sentences.en: After years of fighting, the rebels succeeded.
sentences.zh: 经过多年的战斗，叛军取得了成功。

sentences.en: They created the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了美洲合众国。

sentences.en: You can listen to my episode about this that I released at the beginning of July, maybe three or four weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 大家可以去听听我在七月初发布的关于这段历史的那期节目，大概是三四周前吧。

sentences.en: But not everyone living in the new United States supported the revolution.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有生活在新美国的人都支持这场革命。

sentences.en: Many people there remained loyal to the British Crown.
sentences.zh: 那里有许多人依然效忠英国王室。

sentences.en: Once the US became independent, those loyal people decided to leave the new United States.
sentences.zh: 一旦美国宣告独立，那些忠诚的人便决定离开这个新兴的美洲国家。

sentences.en: And many of these people headed north. Tens of thousands of English-speaking Loyalists, people loyal to Britain, settled in other parts of British North America.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人向北进发。数以万计的英语保皇党人——即效忠英国的人——在英属北美的其他地区定居下来。

sentences.en: They particularly moved to what is now Ontario, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia.
sentences.zh: 他们主要搬到了现在的安大略省、新不伦瑞克省和新斯科舍省。

sentences.en: So this meant there were now large English-speaking communities living alongside French-speaking Canadians.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，如今有大量说英语的社群与说法语的加拿大人生活在同一片土地上。

sentences.en: Britain also encouraged further immigration from the British Isles.
sentences.zh: 英国还鼓励来自英伦三岛的进一步移民。

sentences.en: Throughout the 19th century, people arrived from England, Scotland, Ireland, and Wales.
sentences.zh: 在整个19世纪，人们从英格兰、苏格兰、爱尔兰和威尔士来到这里。

sentences.en: One of the most significant migrations came during the Irish potato famine of the 1840s.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的一次人口迁徙发生在1840年代的爱尔兰大饥荒期间。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of Irish immigrants crossed the Atlantic, and many of these people settled in Canada.
sentences.zh: 数十万爱尔兰移民横渡大西洋，其中许多人在加拿大定居。

sentences.en: Canada’s population was really diverse, especially by the standards of the time.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的多元人口结构在当时的标准来看确实十分丰富。

sentences.en: There were the indigenous nations who still had a large amount of territory.
sentences.zh: 有占有大片领土的原住民民族。

sentences.en: There were French-speaking Canadians who were the descendants of the settlers of New France.
sentences.zh: 有作为新法兰西定居者后代的法裔加拿大人。

sentences.en: And there were the English-speaking communities from across Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有来自英国各地的英语社群。

sentences.en: And also an increasing number of immigrants from other parts of Europe, too.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有来自欧洲其他地区的移民数量也在不断增加。

sentences.en: Rather than forcing everyone to adopt a single language or culture, Canada gradually recognized that multiple cultures could exist in one place.
sentences.zh: 加拿大没有强迫所有人采用单一的语言或文化，而是逐渐意识到多种文化可以在同一个地方共存。

sentences.en: They recognized that both English and French could be used as languages.
sentences.zh: 他们承认英语和法语都可以作为通用语言使用。

sentences.en: And today, both English and French are the official languages of Canada at the federal level.
sentences.zh: 而今天，英语和法语都是加拿大联邦层面的官方语言。

sentences.en: That means Canadians have the right to communicate with the federal government, the national government, in either language.
sentences.zh: 这意味着加拿大人有权用其中任何一种语言与联邦政府、国家政府进行沟通。

sentences.en: And their official documents, like passports or parliamentary debates, are available in both languages.
sentences.zh: 他们的官方文件，比如护照或议会辩论记录，都有这两种语言的版本。

sentences.en: This doesn’t mean Canada is fully bilingual or everyone in Canada is bilingual.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着加拿大是完全双语的，或者说加拿大所有的人都是双语者。

sentences.en: Quebec is overwhelmingly French-speaking, and protecting the French language is a really big part of Quebec’s identity.
sentences.zh: 魁北克绝大多数人口都说法语，保护法语是魁北克身份认同中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Quebec has introduced laws to ensure that French is the dominant language in schools, businesses, and public life.
sentences.zh: 魁北克已经出台了相关法律，以确保法语在学校、企业和公共生活中占主导地位。

sentences.en: Most other provinces are primarily English-speaking, although there might be French-speaking communities.
sentences.zh: 其他大多数省份主要说英语，尽管可能也存在一些法语社群。

sentences.en: New Brunswick is Canada’s only officially bilingual province, where English and French have equal legal status.
sentences.zh: 新不伦瑞克省是加拿大唯一的官方双语省份，英语和法语在那里享有同等的法律地位。

sentences.en: Also, more than 70 indigenous languages are spoken across Canada.
sentences.zh: 此外，加拿大各地还讲着70多种原住民语言。

sentences.en: Some of these are spoken by a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 其中一些语言有很多人在使用。

sentences.en: For example, in the northern Canadian province of Nunavut, or territory of Nunavut, 80% of the population speaks a language called Inuktitut, which is an Inuit language.
sentences.zh: 例如，在加拿大北部省份努纳武特（Nunavut）或者说努纳武特地区，80%的人口说一种名为因纽蒂图特语（Inuktitut）的语言，这是一种因纽特语。

sentences.en: It’s important to know that Canada has different languages because I was talking to someone recently, one of my Patreon subscribers, who mentioned that they had gone to Canada with the intention of studying and improving their English, but they went to Montreal.
sentences.zh: 了解加拿大存在不同的语言非常重要，因为我最近在和某个人聊天时——他是我Patreon上的一位订阅者——他提到自己曾带着学习和提高英语的目的去加拿大，但他们去了蒙特利尔。

sentences.en: Montreal is in Quebec, and Montreal is a French-speaking city.
sentences.zh: 蒙特利尔在魁北克，而蒙特利尔是一个说法语的城市。

sentences.en: Although you could probably use English and there will be lots of bilingual people, the major language there is French, not English.
sentences.zh: 尽管你可能也能使用英语，而且会有很多双语人士，但那里的主要语言是法语，而不是英语。

sentences.en: So it’s important to know if you’re visiting Canada, are you going to an English-speaking place or a French-speaking place?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要访问加拿大，弄清楚你是要去一个英语区还是法语区非常重要。

sentences.en: I think a really interesting and relevant question about Canada is why isn’t Canada part of the United States?
sentences.zh: 我认为关于加拿大一个非常有趣且切题的问题是：为什么加拿大不是美国的一部分？

sentences.en: Trump has made comments about Canada becoming part of the US in the past, the 51st state, but why isn’t it already?
sentences.zh: 特朗普过去曾发表过关于加拿大成为美国一部分的言论，即“第五十个州”，但为什么它现在还不是呢？

sentences.en: They share the world’s longest international border.
sentences.zh: 他们共享着世界上最长的国际边界。

sentences.en: The two countries have similar cultures, similar economies, and similar histories.
sentences.zh: 两国有着相似的文化、相似的经济和相似的历史。

sentences.en: They were both former British colonies. So why are they not one country?
sentences.zh: 它们都曾是英国的殖民地。那么为什么它们不是同一个国家呢？

sentences.en: Well, as I mentioned earlier, thousands of loyalists fled the United States because they supported Britain.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，成千上万的保皇党人因为支持英国而逃离了美国。

sentences.en: They moved north to the area that is now Canada because they wanted to be British subjects.
sentences.zh: 他们向北搬到了现在的加拿大地区，因为他们想做英国的子民。

sentences.en: They did not want to be Americans. French-speaking Canadians also had their own reasons for staying loyal.
sentences.zh: 他们不想成为美国人。法裔加拿大人留在原地效忠英国也有他们自己的理由。

sentences.en: The American revolutionaries were English-speaking Protestants.
sentences.zh: 美国的革命者是说英语的新教徒。

sentences.en: French Canadians were not convinced that joining the revolution would be good for them, whereas Britain had promised they could continue being Catholic and speaking French.
sentences.zh: 法裔加拿大人并不确信加入革命对他们会有好处，而英国则曾许诺他们可以继续信奉天主教并说法语。

sentences.en: In 1775, American forces invaded Quebec.
sentences.zh: 1775年，美军入侵魁北克。

sentences.en: The aim was to take control of the province of Quebec and persuade French Canadians to join the revolution.
sentences.zh: 其目的是夺取魁北克省的控制权，并说服法裔加拿大人加入革命。

sentences.en: The invasion failed, and Canada stayed British.
sentences.zh: 这次入侵失败了，加拿大依然归属英国。

sentences.en: 40 years later was the War of 1812. The United States declared war on Britain, and one of its major goals was invading British North America.
sentences.zh: 40年后迎来了1812年战争。美国对英国宣战，其主要目标之一就是入侵英属北美。

sentences.en: Some politicians in the US believed that conquering Canada would be easy.
sentences.zh: 美国的一些政客认为征服加拿大易如反掌。

sentences.en: But they were wrong. British soldiers and the Canadian militia resisted invasion.
sentences.zh: 但他们错了。英国士兵和加拿大地方民兵进行了顽强的抵抗。

sentences.en: Peace was finally agreed in 1814, and the border since then has remained almost exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 双方最终于1814年达成和平协议，自那以后，边境线几乎原封不动地保持到了今天。

sentences.en: The War of 1812 became a really important moment in Canadian history because it was a demonstration that British North America was not the United States.
sentences.zh: 1812年战争成了加拿大历史上一个极其重要的时刻，因为它证明了英属北美不是美国。

sentences.en: And would never be part of the United States.
sentences.zh: 并且永远不会成为美国的一部分。

sentences.en: Canada wasn’t an independent country, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，当时的加拿大并不是一个独立的国家。

sentences.en: Canada was still governed by Britain. It was a set of provinces and colonies stretched across North America.
sentences.zh: 加拿大仍然受英国统治。它只是一组横跨北美的省份和殖民地。

sentences.en: Over the 19th century, that began to change.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，这种情况开始发生改变。

sentences.en: Britain gradually gave colonies more freedom to govern themselves, and then some different problems encouraged provinces and colonies to work together.
sentences.zh: 英国逐渐赋予了殖民地更多自治的自由，随后一些不同的问题促使各省和殖民地开始合作。

sentences.en: One problem was the railways. They wanted to build railways across Canada, and this required colonies working together.
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题就是铁路。他们想要修建横贯加拿大的铁路，这需要各个殖民地通力合作。

sentences.en: There were also concerns about whether the US was going to try and invade again after the Civil War in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪中叶美国内战之后，人们还担忧美国是否会再次试图入侵。

sentences.en: In 1867, four colonies, Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick, joined together to form the Dominion of Canada.
sentences.zh: 1867年，安大略、魁北克、新斯科舍和新不伦瑞克四个殖民地联合起来，组成了加拿大自治领（Dominion of Canada）。

sentences.en: This moment is known as Confederation. Although Canada was part of the British Empire, it now had its own parliament and could govern itself in almost all domestic matters.
sentences.zh: 这一历史时刻被称为“联邦化”（Confederation）。尽管加拿大当时仍是大英帝国的一部分，但它现在拥有了自己的议会，并且在几乎所有内部事务上都可以自主管理。

sentences.en: Over the following decades, more provinces and territories joined the Federation.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，更多的省份和地区加入了联邦。

sentences.en: These are the territories in the north and in the west of the country.
sentences.zh: 这些是位于该国北部和西部的地区。

sentences.en: Even after Confederation, though, Britain still had some power over parts of Canadian life and the Canadian government.
sentences.zh: 不过，即使在联邦化之后，英国对加拿大生活的某些方面以及加拿大政府仍然保留着一些权力。

sentences.en: Canada signed the Statute of Westminster in 1931, which gave it almost complete independence legally from Britain.
sentences.zh: 加拿大在1931年签署了《威斯敏斯特法令》，这在法律上赋予了它从英国获得几乎完全的独立。

sentences.en: Then, in 1982, Canada took the final constitutional step by taking the British Constitution and moving it into Canada.
sentences.zh: 随后，在1982年，加拿大迈出了宪法层面的最后一步，将英国宪法“拿回”并移交给了加拿大。

sentences.en: From 1982 onwards, the British Parliament no longer had any authority to make laws for Canada.
sentences.zh: 从1982年起，英国议会不再拥有为加拿大制定法律的任何权力。

sentences.en: Canada was now in control of its constitution.
sentences.zh: 加拿大现在完全掌控了自己的宪法。

sentences.en: But, Canada still has a king. And their king is King Charles, the same king as the United Kingdom has.
sentences.zh: 但是，加拿大依然有一个国王。他们的国王是查尔斯国王，也就是英国现任的同一位国王。

sentences.en: When a new government is formed in Canada, the Prime Minister is invited to form a government by the Governor General, who is the representative of the King.
sentences.zh: 当加拿大组建新政府时，首相会应总督（Governor General）的邀请去组阁，而总督正是国王的代表。

sentences.en: Canadian passports mention the King. New members of Parliament swear an oath to the King.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的护照上提到了国王。新当选的议员们也要向国王宣誓效忠。

sentences.en: There is something important here, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这里有一点非常重要。

sentences.en: The King of the United Kingdom is not the King of Canada.
sentences.zh: 英国国王并不只是英国的国王。

sentences.en: The King of the United Kingdom is also the King of Canada.
sentences.zh: 英国的国王同时也是加拿大的国王。

sentences.en: He has separate jobs. When King Charles III performs his duties in Britain, he is the King of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他有着不同的职责。当查尔斯三世国王在英国履行职责时，他是英国国王。

sentences.en: But when he performs duties related to Canada, he is the King of Canada, and he follows the advice of the Canadian prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但当他履行与加拿大相关的职责时，他是加拿大国王，并且他要遵循加拿大首相的建议。

sentences.en: He has two completely separate roles. In fact, he has more roles.
sentences.zh: 他拥有两个完全独立的身份。事实上，他的身份还不止两个。

sentences.en: He’s also the king of Australia and New Zealand and other places, too.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是澳大利亚、新西兰及其他地方的国王。

sentences.en: Britain cannot tell Canada what to do. The British Parliament has no power over Canadian laws.
sentences.zh: 英国无权对加拿大指手画脚。英国议会对加拿大的法律没有管辖权。

sentences.en: The British prime minister has no role in the Canadian government.
sentences.zh: 英国首相在加拿大政府中没有任何角色。

sentences.en: Canada is completely sovereign. But they have a king, and that king happens to also be the King of England.
sentences.zh: 加拿大是完全主权独立的。但他们有一位国王，而这位国王恰好也是英国的国王。

sentences.en: What does the king actually do, though? In practice, not really anything.
sentences.zh: 不过，国王实际上做些什么呢？在实践中，其实什么也不做。

sentences.en: Like the British monarch, Canada’s monarch is almost entirely a ceremonial figure.
sentences.zh: 和英国君主一样，加拿大的君主几乎完全是一个象征性的虚位元首。

sentences.en: The day-to-day running of the country is carried out by elected politicians led by a prime minister.
sentences.zh: 国家的日常运作是由以首相为首的民选政治家来执行的。

sentences.en: The monarch, the King’s, responsibilities include opening Parliament, appointing governors, and giving assent to new laws, giving their permission for new laws to be made.
sentences.zh: 君主即国王的职责包括：主持议会开幕、任命总督，以及批准新法律、给予新法案颁布实施的许可。

sentences.en: In Canada, these roles are usually performed by the governor general, the King’s representative in Canada, and they are mainly ceremonial.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，这些职责通常由总督（即国王在加拿大的代表）来履行，而且这些职责主要都是礼仪性的。

sentences.en: For example, a bill passed by Canada’s Parliament does not become law officially until it receives Royal Assent, permission from the King.
sentences.zh: 例如，加拿大议会通过的一项法案，直到正式获得“御准”（Royal Assent，即国王的批准）后，才会正式成为法律。

sentences.en: This is always a formality. The governor general acts according to the advice of Canada’s elected government.
sentences.zh: 这通常只是一种例行程序。总督会根据加拿大民选政府的建议行事。

sentences.en: So if the government wants something, the King will do it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果政府想要做某事，国王就会照办。

sentences.en: Canada’s political system is therefore very similar to Britain’s.
sentences.zh: 因此，加拿大的政治制度与英国非常相似。

sentences.en: Both countries use the Westminster parliamentary system.
sentences.zh: 两国都采用威斯敏斯特议会制。

sentences.en: This is where voters elect members of Parliament, and the leader of the largest party in Parliament usually is the prime minister, and the King is politically neutral.
sentences.zh: 在这种制度下，选民选举议会议员，议会中最大政党的领袖通常担任首相，而国王则在政治上保持中立。

sentences.en: Not everyone thinks Canada should be a monarchy.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都认为加拿大应该保留君主制。

sentences.en: Some Canadians see it as a outdated thing.
sentences.zh: 一些加拿大人认为这是一种过时的东西。

sentences.en: Why should an independent country like Canada have a monarch who lives thousands of kilometers away in London and rarely visits Canada?
sentences.zh: 为什么像加拿大这样一个独立的国，还要有一个远在几千公里外的伦敦居住、且极少访问加拿大的君主呢？

sentences.en: They believe that Canada should become a republic with its own Canadian head of state.
sentences.zh: 他们认为加拿大应该转变为一个共和国，拥有属于自己的加拿大国家元首。

sentences.en: This debate does receive attention from time to time in Canada, but it isn’t a issue that dominates Canadian politics.
sentences.zh: 这种争论在加拿大确实不时受到关注，但它并非主导加拿大政坛的核心议题。

sentences.en: People tend to care more about healthcare, housing, immigration, the economy.
sentences.zh: 人们往往更关心医疗保健、住房、移民和经济问题。

sentences.en: The royal family doesn’t really matter to most voters.
sentences.zh: 皇室对于大多数选民来说其实并不那么重要。

sentences.en: Today, Canada sees itself as a country built through immigration.
sentences.zh: 如今，加拿大将自己视为一个通过移民建立起来的国家。

sentences.en: It doesn’t necessarily see itself as a former British or former French colony.
sentences.zh: 它不一定把自己看作是一个前英国或前法国的殖民地。

sentences.en: That’s not what its identity is. For example, nearly one in four Canadians right now were born in another country.
sentences.zh: 这并不是它的国家认同所在。例如，现在差不多每四个加拿大人中就有一个出生在另一个国家。

sentences.en: This is one of the highest proportions anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上比例最高的国家之一。

sentences.en: 25% of Canada was not born in Canada. It has one of the highest immigration rates in the Western world.
sentences.zh: 25%的加拿大人并非出生在加拿大。它拥有西方世界最高的移民率之一。

sentences.en: If you walk through Toronto or Vancouver, you will find neighborhoods of Chinese, Indian, Filipino, Italian, Caribbean, Middle Eastern, African, and Latin American communities.
sentences.zh: 如果你走过多伦多或温哥华，你会发现由华人、印度人、菲律宾人、意大利人、加勒比人、中东人、非洲人和拉丁美洲人组成的社区。

sentences.en: This diversity is not an accident. Canada has always been a nation of immigration.
sentences.zh: 这种多元性并非偶然。加拿大一直是一个移民国家。

sentences.en: Originally, the immigration policies in Canada favored British people, and then people from Northern Europe.
sentences.zh: 最初，加拿大的移民政策偏袒英国人，然后是北欧人。

sentences.en: In some cases, they actually restricted immigration from other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们实际上限制了来自世界其他地区的移民。

sentences.en: An infamous example is the Chinese Head Tax, which was introduced in the late 19th century to discourage Chinese immigration.
sentences.zh: 一个声名狼籍的例子就是“人头税”（Chinese Head Tax），这是在19世纪后期引入的，旨在阻碍华人移民。

sentences.en: Even though thousands of Chinese workers had helped build Canada’s railways, the government didn’t want them to stay living there.
sentences.zh: 尽管成千上万的中国劳工曾帮助建设加拿大的铁路，但政府并不希望他们留下来生活。

sentences.en: From the 1960s onwards, though, Canada transformed its immigration system.
sentences.zh: 不过，从20世纪60年代开始，加拿大对其移民系统进行了彻底改造。

sentences.en: It has a points-based immigration system.
sentences.zh: 它推行了一套基于积分的移民系统。

sentences.en: They award points to potential immigrants based on factors like education, work experience, language ability, and professional skills.
sentences.zh: 他们根据教育程度、工作经验、语言能力和专业技能等因素对潜在移民进行评分。

sentences.en: The goal was to attract talented people who could contribute to Canada’s economy.
sentences.zh: 其目标是吸引能够为加拿大经济做出贡献的杰出人才。

sentences.en: Many of Canada’s largest immigrant communities now come from countries like India, China, the Philippines, Nigeria, Pakistan, and many others.
sentences.zh: 如今，加拿大许多最大的移民社群都来自印度、中国、菲律宾、尼日利亚、巴基斯坦等众多国家。

sentences.en: Canada is one of the most ethnically and culturally diverse societies in the world.
sentences.zh: 加拿大是世界上种族和文化最多元化的社会之一。

sentences.en: Alongside immigration, Canada has also followed a policy of multiculturalism.
sentences.zh: 除了移民，加拿大还奉行多元文化主义政策。

sentences.en: Canada officially encourages people to keep their own cultural heritage and their own languages while becoming Canadian.
sentences.zh: 加拿大官方鼓励人们在成为加拿大人同时，保留自己的文化遗产和母语。

sentences.en: Of course, people continue to question whether this is a successful policy.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们一直在质疑这是否是一项成功的政策。

sentences.en: Is multiculturalism successful really? But it is one of the country’s most important and most defining values.
sentences.zh: 多元文化主义真的成功吗？但它是该国最重要、最具定义性的价值观之一。

sentences.en: Economically, Canada is also one of the world’s wealthiest nations.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，加拿大也是世界上最富裕的国家之一。

sentences.en: It has a lot of natural resources. It produces oil, natural gas, timber, minerals, agricultural products.
sentences.zh: 它拥有丰富的自然资源。它生产石油、天然气、木材、矿产和农产品。

sentences.en: It is one of the world’s largest exporters of wheat, potash, and uranium.
sentences.zh: 它是世界最大的小麦、钾肥和铀出口国之一。

sentences.en: And Alberta’s oil sands contain some of the largest oil reserves on Earth.
sentences.zh: 阿尔伯塔省的油砂蕴藏着地球上规模最大的石油储量之一。

sentences.en: Cities like Toronto are major financial centers.
sentences.zh: 像多伦多这样的城市是主要的金融中心。

sentences.en: Montreal has become a place recognized for its aerospace and artificial intelligence industries.
sentences.zh: 蒙特利尔已成为一个以航空航天和人工智能产业闻名的城市。

sentences.en: Vancouver is a place of technology and film production and international trade with Asia.
sentences.zh: 温哥华则是科技、影视制作以及与亚洲开展国际贸易的重镇。

sentences.en: Because Canada shares a long border with the United States, the two countries’ economies are interconnected.
sentences.zh: 由于加拿大与美国共享漫长的边境线，两国的经济是紧密相连的。

sentences.en: Every day, billions of dollars of goods and services cross the border.
sentences.zh: 每天都有价值数十亿美元的商品和服务跨越边境。

sentences.en: Canada is the largest trading partner of the United States by far.
sentences.zh: 加拿大是美国最大的贸易伙伴，而且远远领先于其他国家。

sentences.en: Internationally, Canada has a reputation as a stable democracy and as a middle power.
sentences.zh: 在国际上，加拿大享有稳定民主政体和中等强国的声誉。

sentences.en: There are a lot of challenges in Canada, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，加拿大也面临着许多挑战。

sentences.en: Housing is really expensive. The cost of living has risen sharply.
sentences.zh: 住房价格非常昂贵。生活成本急剧上升。

sentences.en: Indigenous communities continue to seek justice for the horrific and historic abuses they suffered.
sentences.zh: 原住民社群仍在为他们所遭受的可怕历史虐待寻求正义。

sentences.en: And there are now many debates over immigration, identity, climate change, and economic growth.​
sentences.zh: 如今围绕移民、身份认同、气候变化和经济增长也存在着许多辩论。​

sentences.en: What might Canada look like in another 50 years?
sentences.zh: 再过50年，加拿大可能会是什么样子？

sentences.en: One possibility is that it becomes even more diverse.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是它变得更加多元化。

sentences.en: Canada’s population will keep growing, largely because of immigration.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的总人口将继续增长，这主要归功于移民。

sentences.en: But whether Canada will be successful depends on if it can build enough homes, schools, infrastructure to support population growth.
sentences.zh: 但加拿大能否取得成功，取决于它能否建造足够的住房、学校和基础设施来支撑人口增长。

sentences.en: Immigration has definitely been one of Canada’s strengths, but it can only continue being a strength if Canada can offer a high quality of life to everyone.
sentences.zh: 移民绝对是加拿大的优势之一，但只有当加拿大能够为每个人提供高质量的生活时，它才能继续成为一种优势。

sentences.en: Climate change will also really influence Canada’s future.
sentences.zh: 气候变化也将真正影响加拿大的未来。

sentences.en: It’s one of the world’s largest countries and has really been affected by climate change already.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最大的国家之一，而且已经深受气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: Temperatures are rising. There are more wildfires, changing weather patterns.
sentences.zh: 气温正在上升。山火更多了，天气模式也在改变。

sentences.en: Canada also has the Arctic, which could really change due to climate change.
sentences.zh: 加拿大还拥有北极地区，该地区可能会因气候变化而发生剧烈改变。

sentences.en: Another important question is about what it means to be Canada.
sentences.zh: 另一个重要问题是，成为加拿大究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: For much of its history, Canada has defined itself through its relationship with France and Britain and now maybe perhaps with the United States.
sentences.zh: 在其历史的大部分时间里，加拿大一直通过它与法国和英国的关系来定义自己，而现在或许又加上了与美国的关系。

sentences.en: Modern Canada is indigenous. It is French-speaking.
sentences.zh: 现代的加拿大是原住民的。,它是说法语的。

sentences.en: It is English-speaking. It’s multicultural.
sentences.zh: 它是说英语的。它是多元文化的。

sentences.en: It is a country of immigration from almost every place on Earth.
sentences.zh: 它是一个几乎从地球上所有地方吸收移民的国家。

sentences.en: Canada’s identity is not based on a single history or a single language or a single ethnicity.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的身份认同并非建立在单一的历史、单一的语言或单一的族裔之上。

sentences.en: It is the idea that many different identities can exist within the same country.
sentences.zh: 它是这样一种理念：许多不同的身份认同可以共存于同一个国家之内。

sentences.en: Can this continue? Can Canada continue protecting French while also having English as its main language?
sentences.zh: 这种情况能持续下去吗？加拿大能否在把英语作为主要语言的同时，继续保护法语？

sentences.en: Can it remain open to immigration? Can it balance its economic growth with environmental responsibility?
sentences.zh: 它能对移民保持开放吗？它能在经济增长与环境责任之间取得平衡吗？

sentences.en: These are really difficult questions, and there are no easy answers.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常棘手的问题，而且没有简单的答案。

sentences.en: But what do you think? What do you think about Canada?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你对加拿大有什么看法？

sentences.en: Have you ever visited Canada? Do you want to visit?
sentences.zh: 你曾经去过加拿大吗？你想去吗？

sentences.en: Let me know what people in your country think about Canada.
sentences.zh: 让我知道你们国家的人是怎么看待加拿大的。

sentences.en: Do you have any stereotypes about Canada?
sentences.zh: 你对加拿大有什么刻板印象吗？
